chunks: Ahmad narrated from Amr ibn Uthman from Ali ibn Abdullah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to say: 'O group of those who have not performed Hajj, receive glad tidings with the pilgrs, shake their hands, and magnify them, for that is obligatory upon you so that you may share with them in the reward.'
ai.seo_question: What should those who did not perform Hajj do to share in the reward of the pilgrims?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS) instructs those who could not perform Hajj to rejoice in the success of the pilgrims, shake their hands, and honor them, as this act is obligatory and allows them to share in the pilgrims' reward. This narration highlights the Shia concept of *shirkah fi al-ajr* (sharing in reward), where the spiritual merit of Hajj extends to the community through the recognition and celebration of those who performed it, reinforcing social cohesion and collective piety.
